title: Billing API authorization middleware and routes
name: Billing API routes

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these routes decide whether the caller may access a given record? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A caller whose token has roles ["billing_admin"] and scope "invoices:read" only sends POST /payments/:id/refunds for a payment in their own account. What is the response?
choices: 201, because billing_admin is sufficient to issue refunds.
403 with insufficient_scope, because requireScope("refunds:write") fails after the role check passes.
401, because the token lacks the refund scope.
404, because the payment lookup does not find the record.

questions.prompt: GET /invoices/:invoiceId for an invoice that exists but belongs to another account returns 404 rather than 403. What is the effect of that choice?
choices: It avoids disclosing whether an invoice ID exists in other accounts, since a missing record and a foreign record look identical.
It reveals that the invoice exists but is off limits to the caller.
It is a bug because 404 is only for routes that do not exist.
It lets the caller retry with a different token to obtain access.

questions.prompt: A user with only the "viewer" role and the token scope "invoices:read" calls each endpoint for resources in their own account. Which calls succeed?
choices: None of them, because every route needs a role
All of them, because the account matches
